invariants: Every application source file belongs to exactly one declared source boundary.
First-party imports follow the declared directional allowlist.
Renderer code imports neither Electron nor Node modules.
Preload code exposes typed contract methods and never generic IPC authority.

Main coordinates application lifecycle and holds no execution, signing, credential, database, policy, journal, approval, grant, VM, process-launch, service-configuration, or peer-requirement authority.
Main may define only an uncomposed typed test client for INSPECT, STOP_ONE, and STOP_ALL; it cannot register, configure, or discover the service.
Policy code imports only governed contracts, emits no authoritative wire decision, and holds no effect authority.
The isolated grant proof helper can create only service-local test approvals and one-use no-effect grants after exact policy, binding, durable acknowledgement, key, and assurance checks.
Execution-grant v1 remains a D5 envelope; only module-private proof-service state can consume it, and no proof result can invoke or represent an effect.
Emergency stop in the proof helper is audit-independent, idempotent, and reduce-only; it returns no execution authority.

The isolated audit helper writes only its canonical journal, exposes only an injected capsule-registry binding port to Main, and can sign only a freshly verified bounded checkpoint through a module-private software test fixture.
The capsule-registry binding port exposes no journal instance, database handle, source credential, generic append operation, signing operation, or reconciliation authority.
The packaged Secure Enclave proof helper has no Electron transport, production checkpoint API, arbitrary-message signing API, database access, or network authority.

Secure Enclave lifecycle and recovery cleanup operations require explicit owner authorization, are restricted to one UUID-derived proof-only application-tag namespace, and verify exact-tag deletion before success; signing is limited to one internally constructed challenge.

The inert execution-service fixture mutates only embedded fixture records through INSPECT, STOP_ONE, and STOP_ALL and accepts no PID, path, executable, arguments, environment, mount, socket, network, VM-start, or arbitrary payload field.
The execution-service fixture has no registration, XPC listener, application composition, VM, process-launch, filesystem, network, reconciliation, journal, ownership-release, or production authority.
A framework inspection fixture outside the native-helper root cannot create or start a VM, launch a process, access a filesystem, consume standard input, or contact a network.
No implemented helper can contact an anchor or label evidence ANCHORED without offline verification under independently obtained trust material.
Application source cannot import native-helper implementations; Main may invoke only contracts admitted by an accepted generation after their separate composition gates are accepted.
Workers accept bounded validated data and hold no effect authority.
Reserved native-helper roots contain no executable code before their owner phase and a separate accepted ownership update.
Renderer source satisfies docs/architecture/renderer-authority-policy-v1.json with no authority finding.
